<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
          <jats:p>Wythoff Nim is a classical combinatorial game of queen moves on a chessboard. There are many ways to describe its <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>-positions (safe positions to move to). One way is to code them by the Fibonacci word 010010100100101..., which is the unique fixed point of the substitution of 0 by 01, and of 1 by 0. The coordinates of the <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>-th <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>-position are encoded by the location of the <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>-th zero and the <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>-th one in the Fibonacci word. We show that a minor modification of the rules of Wythoff Nim leads to a game with <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>-positions that are coded by 010010010010100100... This word can be derived by deleting all 2’s from the Tribonacci word, which is the unique fixed point of the substitution of 0 by 01, of 1 by 02, and of 2 by 0.</jats:p>
title: Queen reflections: a modification of Wythoff Nim

readings.abstract: Abstract:We modify Wythoff's game by allowing an additional move, which we call a "split", and show how the $P$-positions are coded by the Tribonacci word. We analyze the table of letter positions of arbitrary $k$-bonacci words and find a $\mathrm{mex}$-rule that generates the Quadribonacci table.
